bug_semantics: With the default allow_unsafe_options=False, a caller-controlled kwargs mapping can set split_single_char_options=False and a one-character key such as n with value "utouch /tmp/ACE;git-upload-pack". GitPython 3.1.57's Git._option_candidates checks only -n because value-derived candidates are gated on split_single_char_options being true, while Git.transform_kwarg emits the joined token -nutouch /tmp/ACE;git-upload-pack. Git parses clustered short options inside that token, reaches -u/--upload-pack with an attacker-selected helper command, and executes it even though the guarded API (for example Repo.clone_from) did not opt into unsafe options.
flaw_origin: Commit e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 was an incomplete security fix: it first added split_single_char_options = kwargs.get(..., True) and the conditional `if len(key) == 1 and split_single_char_options` to Git._option_candidates in git/cmd.py. That conditional added value candidates for the split form but deliberately left the unsplit compatibility path represented only by the short key, despite transform_kwarg already serializing that path as a joined -<key><value> token. The commit's own new test recorded the mismatch for split_single_char_options=False by expecting transform_kwargs to produce -n--upload-pack=helper while _option_candidates returned only -n.
